subject.title: Cron session accumulation can silently exhaust agent context window — no guardrails or warnings

question: Should #38730 stay open as the canonical umbrella until OpenClaw accepts a cron cadence guardrail and guarded cron-session retention cleanup, with #89739's cron.minInterval as the preferred high-frequency contract?
rationale: The source-backed gaps are real, but closing depends on maintainer choices about a new core config surface and which persisted cron base sessions are disposable under retention.

options.title: Accept #89739 plus guarded retention path
options.body: Use #89739 for configurable recurring-cadence enforcement and #90194 or an equivalent guarded fix for stale orphan/base cron session cleanup before closing the umbrella.

options.title: Split remaining work now
options.body: Keep the concrete retention issue under #89666 and create narrower follow-ups for context threshold warnings or sessions cleanup, then close #38730 only after the split is complete.

options.title: Reject core cadence config
options.body: If maintainers do not want cron.minInterval in core, close or redirect #89739 and choose a warning-only or documentation-only policy for the high-frequency guardrail slice.

recommendation.title: Accept #89739 plus guarded retention path
recommendation.body: Use #89739 for configurable recurring-cadence enforcement and #90194 or an equivalent guarded fix for stale orphan/base cron session cleanup before closing the umbrella.

likelyOwner.reason: amknight owns the current cron.minInterval proposal and already made the maintainer decision that #38730 remains canonical for high-frequency cron guardrails.
